items.label_en: 1. Draw: King Inside the Pawn's Square
items.explanation_en: The black king is inside the square of the a-pawn and catches it before promotion.

items.label_en: 2. Win: King Outside the Pawn's Square
items.explanation_en: The black king starts outside the square and cannot catch the pawn as the square shrinks.
Mirror the white king's moves to hold the opposition and deny access to the key squares.
Advance the pawn to force the black king to move, then take the flank route to the key squares and promote.
The black king mirrors White's moves and maintains the opposition to hold the draw.
Take the distant opposition, shorten the distance, reach the key squares, and escort the pawn to promotion.
Use opposition to reach a8 and prevent the a-pawn from promoting without stalemate or capture.

items.label_en: 1. Decoy the King with Opposite-Wing Pawns
items.explanation_en: Use the h-pawn as a decoy so the b-pawn can promote beyond the black king's reach.
Calculate the tempi accurately and coordinate the king with the connected pawns to promote.
The f-pawn ties the black king to f8 while the h-pawn advances as a second threat.
Use Kc7 to support the c-pawn and drive the black king away from the key squares.
Take the opposition with the king to drive the defender away from the d-file and advance the pawn safely.
The kings mirror each other while the pawns are locked, and neither side can advance without losing a pawn.
The black king returns in time to defend, showing that king activity alone does not guarantee a win.
With the black king far away, go around the pawn blockade, take the opposition, and win the pawn.
Capture the opposing passed pawn, then use the king to escort your own pawn to promotion.

items.label_en: 1. Blockade and Win the Isolated Pawn
items.explanation_en: The connected d-pawns hold the black d-pawn while the white king captures the isolated g-pawn.

items.label_en: 2. Advance Connected Pawns with the King
items.explanation_en: The king leads the g- and h-pawns forward together, creating two promotion routes.
Restrict the black king and advance the connected pawns to create threats on both files.

items.label_en: 4. Win the Race on Opposite Wings
items.explanation_en: Sacrifice the a-pawn if necessary and push the c-pawn, which promotes first.
Promote the a-pawn at once, then use the queen and g-pawn to remove Black's counterplay.
Use a checking pawn advance to draw the king away, then push the connected b- and c-pawns to create two promotion threats.

items.label_en: 2. Use the King to Support Three Pawns
items.explanation_en: The advanced king cuts off the defender while three connected pawns advance together.

items.label_en: 3. Distract with an Outside Passed Pawn
items.explanation_en: The outside f-pawn draws the black king away while the g- and h-pawns break through.

items.label_en: 4. Break Through with a Pawn Exchange
items.explanation_en: Use f5 to force an exchange and expose the black pawns to the white king.

items.label_en: 5. Check and Remove the Key Pawn
items.explanation_en: Advance with check to capture the g-pawn, exchange the remaining defender, and promote the connected pawns.
Support the g-passed pawn with the king while the black king cannot cover both wings.
The advanced white king supports the pawns, enabling a b-pawn breakthrough and multiple passed pawns.

items.label_en: 3. Break Symmetry with the First Move
items.explanation_en: Use 1. b4 to create a passed pawn and force Black into a passive defense.

items.label_en: 4. Stop the Passed Pawn, Advance Your Own
items.explanation_en: Use the king to capture Black's most dangerous passed pawn, then advance the white passed pawns.

items.label_en: 5. King Position Decides the Symmetrical Structure
items.explanation_en: Use the more advanced king to break the symmetry and create a passed b-pawn.
